newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-ARGENTINA'S ZABALETA DEFAULTS AT LIPTON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ARGENTINA'S ZABALETA DEFAULTS AT LIPTON.

text.p: Mariano Zabaleta, Argentina's new hope for tennis stardom, made an early exit from the Lipton Championships on Thursday when he was defaulted near the end of his first-round match, depriving him of his dream of playing Pete Sampras.

Zabaleta, 19 years old and ranked 99th in the world, stood at 6-6 in the third set and was leading 2-1 in the tiebreaker against Romania's Adrian Voinea when he swatted a ball in anger after netting a return of an approach shot.
The ball accidentally struck a linesman in the chest and the umpire called a default despite protests from both players. Voinea also asked the umpire if the match could continue.
Zabaleta apologised to the linesperson and umpire, to no avail. Tournament referee Alan Mills was summoned to the court and supported the umpire's decision.
Zabaleta had been looking forward to playing against Sampras, the top seed and world number one, in the next round.
"The possibility of playing Sampras is a like a dream," said Zabaleta.
"It wouldn't have mattered if I had lost 6-0 6-0 against Sampras, it would have been a dream to play him," Zabaleta said. "I'm very sad about the default because I was winning the match."

Zabaleta, playing only his second year on the tour, said his problem might have been unfamiliarity with this kind of situation: "Maybe I don't have much experience. I only ever got one warning all last year."
